title: Do Diffusion Models Learn to Generalize Basic Visual Skills?
abstract: arXiv:2611.22427v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Diffusion models generate high-quality images, but how well they generalize is hard to measure. Current evaluations rely on human preference and prompt-following benchmarks for text-to-image models and on distribution-level metrics such as Fr\'echet Inception Distance (FID) and Inception Score (IS) for class-conditional models, but these cannot tell whether models learn basic visual skills or largely match training patterns. To address this gap, we introduce the Visual Generative Lab (VGL), a controlled experimental framework for studying how diffusion models learn and generalize basic visual skills, including size, position, rotation, count, color, shape, and their compositions. By generating synthetic training data for each skill from explicit rules, VGL allows precise measurement of generalization with task-specific, rule-based metrics. translated_title: 扩散模型能学会泛化基础视觉技能吗？

tldr: 该论文提出视觉生成实验室（VGL）受控实验框架，通过基于规则生成的合成数据和任务特定指标，首次精确测量扩散模型对大小、位置、旋转、数量、颜色、形状等基础视觉技能的泛化能力，并揭示模型学习中的三种模式。
en_tdlr: The paper introduces the Visual Generative Lab (VGL), a controlled experimental framework that uses rule-based synthetic data and task-specific metrics to precisely measure how diffusion models generalize basic visual skills such as size, position, rotation, count, color, and shape, revealing three patterns in their learning.
